title: Open agent harness powers a second vendor's first-party agent by Q4 2026
body: An open-source agent harness becoming the embedded engine inside a branded first-party vendor agent is on track to repeat at a second major vendor by Q4 2026, confirming that the open core wrapped in proprietary governance is a structural pattern rather than a one-off. Microsoft's Build keynote this week made the shape explicit: Microsoft Scout, the company's first always-on "Autopilot" personal work agent embedded in Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, and SharePoint, is powered by OpenClaw, the open-source local-agent platform and one of the three open coding/agent harnesses this brief tracks. Microsoft did not fork OpenClaw into a hidden internal stack; it shipped the open harness as the runtime and layered enterprise controls on top, so each Scout agent runs under a governed Entra identity with scoped credentials and audit trails, a continuous policy-conformance check, Purview data-protection enforcement before data leaves, and a Work IQ context layer. The reason this generalizes is that the hard, differentiated work for an enterprise vendor is now the governance wrapper, identity, and product surface, while the agent loop itself is a solved, battle-tested open component a vendor can adopt rather than rebuild. That inverts the old build-versus-buy calculus for the engine: reimplementing a proprietary agent runtime offers little advantage over embedding a maintained open harness and competing on controls and distribution. The forward state to watch is therefore a second first-party branded agent from a major platform or productivity vendor that discloses one of the tracked open harnesses (OpenClaw or a peer) as its underlying runtime, wrapped in that vendor's own identity, policy, and data-governance controls. The confirming signal is a launch, preview, or technical disclosure naming a specific open harness as the engine inside a branded enterprise agent; the pattern fails to confirm if rival vendors instead ship agents on closed in-house runtimes through year end.

reasoning.because: Microsoft shipped Scout, an always-on M365 Autopilot agent, powered by open-source OpenClaw
reasoning.given: Scout ships the open harness as runtime and competes on Entra/Purview/policy, not the agent loop
reasoning.so_that: A second major vendor ships a first-party branded agent disclosing a tracked open harness as its engine
reasoning.landing: by Q4 2026; a 2nd branded enterprise agent naming OpenClaw or a peer harness
reasoning.plain_language: Microsoft's new work agent runs on open-source agent software and adds its own controls, so another big company will soon do the same.

summary: Microsoft's Scout, an always-on M365 Autopilot agent, runs on the open-source OpenClaw harness wrapped in Entra and Purview controls. With the agent loop now a solved open component and the edge in the governance wrapper, expect a second vendor to ship a branded agent on an open harness by Q4 2026.
